scenes.title: Receive on the far shoulder
scenes.objective: Receive away from pressure while keeping both the passer and next option available.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). F1 has the puck in the left defensive zone and is preparing a pass. YOU are near the left blue line, farther up ice than F1 and closer to the side boards than D1. F2 is farther up ice as a possible next option.
cues: F1 has the puck and is preparing a pass.
D1 is farther up ice than YOU and closer to the middle.
F2 is farther up ice as a possible next option.

questions.prompt: Who owns the puck before F1 releases it?

options.text: F1
YOU
D1

questions.explanation: The puck owner is stated as F1; the receiving picture does not transfer possession early.

questions.prompt: Which two current relationships should YOU account for when offering a receiving target?

options.text: F1 is behind YOU toward Navy’s defending end
D1 is ahead of YOU and nearer the middle
F2 is behind YOU on the same up-ice side as F1

questions.explanation: The pass comes from F1 behind YOU, while D1 is ahead and inside. F2 is farther up ice, not behind YOU, and remains a possible next connection to check. These positions help plan a receiving angle; they do not prove either pass is available.

questions.prompt: Arrange this receiving decision.

options.text: Scan behind and inside
Present a reachable target to F1
Receive under control and choose the next option

questions.explanation: The scan informs the target, then the touch can be adjusted to the pressure and the available continuation.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a receiving point with more separation from D1 and a visible lane from F1.
questions.explanation: This point changes the angle from F1 and gives D1 a different relationship; the pass still needs to be reachable.

questions.prompt: D1 steps into your inside shoulder as F1 releases. Which reception fits the changed cue?

options.text: Open your body to protect the puck and keep a return option
Turn fully up ice before the puck arrives
Demand the same forward turn even if the lane is covered

questions.explanation: D1 has removed the easy inside turn, so a protected touch and a conditional return preserve more choices.

questions.prompt: Why can a wider receiving angle help here, and what would make you change it?
questions.explanation: A wider angle can separate YOU from D1 while preserving F1's lane. Change it if D1 follows or F1 loses a clean route, then re-offer a reachable option.

scenes.title: Support the carrier after a give-and-go look
scenes.objective: Keep supporting when the first pass changes the puck carrier and the return lane is shaded.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). YOU have just passed to F2; D1 is on the direct return line between you. F1 is on the other side of the middle of the rink and may offer another option.
cues: D1 shades the old return line.
F1 is a visible alternate support player.

questions.prompt: What changed when the pass reached F2?

options.text: F2 became the puck carrier
YOU became the puck carrier again
D1 became a teammate

questions.explanation: The setup assigns the puck to F2, so your job is now support and scanning.

questions.prompt: Which two details should shape your next support spot?

options.text: F2's current puck position
D1's relationship to the old return line
Where the earlier pass started, without checking the new carrier

questions.explanation: F2 and D1 help you judge whether to change your support angle. Recheck the available space; a return pass is only one possible continuation.

questions.prompt: Arrange this post-pass support read.

options.text: Find F2 and the shaded line
Look for a new support angle with separation
Re-check F2, D1 and F1

questions.explanation: Read the carrier and coverage before changing your angle, then recheck. F1 may offer another option if a lane is available.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the side boards to offer a new angle to F2.
questions.explanation: The example adds width and moves the direct return line away from D1. Recheck the passing lane and F1; the new angle does not guarantee an available pass.

questions.prompt: F2 has two Navy support options. Which direct passing line currently stays farther from D1?

options.text: The line from F2’s puck to YOU
The line from F2’s puck to F1

questions.explanation: The line to F1 stays farther from D1 than the old line back to YOU. F2 can assess that alternative while YOU continue offering support. A larger gap from D1 does not guarantee a pass, and YOU may become useful again as the carrier or defender moves.

questions.prompt: What can your support accomplish when F2 keeps the puck?
questions.explanation: It can pull D1, offer a second lane, or protect F2's next option. Describe the named space and make the benefit conditional on D1's response.

scenes.title: Bank the puck off the wall
scenes.objective: Use a wall option to change the route around a defender, then read the rebound.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). F1 owns the puck between the middle and the side boards. D1 is near the direct route to YOU, who are farther up ice and wider. F2 is closer to the middle; D2 is farther toward the right net. A bank off the side boards is one possible route to assess.
cues: D1 is near the direct passing route.
YOU are farther up ice and wider than D1.
F2 is closer to the middle; D2 may affect that option.

questions.prompt: Which defender is nearest the direct F1-to-YOU passing route?

options.text: D1
D2
Neither defender is near that route

questions.explanation: D1 is near the line between F1 and YOU. The freeze does not prove stick reach or an interception.

questions.prompt: Which two details matter before using the wall?

options.text: Where the rebound would leave YOU and D1
Whether the inside option to F2 stays clear of D2
That the wall sends the puck to the same spot every time

questions.explanation: The wall changes the route but not the need to read the rebound, pressure, and inside support.

questions.prompt: Arrange a wall-option plan.

options.text: See D1 and the wall space
Choose a reachable bank point
Read the rebound before the next touch

questions.explanation: The route around D1 is only useful if the rebound and next lane remain controllable.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the side boards, farther up ice than D1, to offer a possible bank-pass target.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU closer to the side boards and farther up ice than D1. F1 still needs to judge a reachable bank point and rebound; no bounce or completed pass is guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Before F1 tries the wall option, which direct passing line is farther from D1 and worth comparing with it?

options.text: The line from F1’s puck to YOU
The line from F1’s puck to F2

questions.explanation: The direct line to F2 stays farther from D1 than the direct line to YOU. F1 can compare it with a possible wall pass, while checking D2 near F2’s area. Neither a direct pass nor a board bounce is proven successful by this freeze.

questions.prompt: How is a wall option different from simply passing through D1?
questions.explanation: It changes the puck route around the defender and creates a new rebound to read. The option remains conditional on the rebound and support.

scenes.title: Open the shooting lane
scenes.objective: Reassess a shooting lane when a defender moves toward another attacker.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). YOU control the puck in the middle of the attacking zone; D1 is between YOU and the net. F2 is wider and farther toward the right goal line. If D1 moves, reassess both the shooting lane and the pass.
cues: D1 occupies the direct shooting line.
F2 is wider and closer to the right goal line than YOU.
The freeze does not prove a shot will reach the net or score.

questions.prompt: Who is between YOU and the right net?

options.text: F2
D1
The goalie only

questions.explanation: D1 is between YOU and the goalie in the direct lane.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should be read together?

options.text: D1's position in the lane
F2's availability if D1 moves
A promise that the lane will clear

questions.explanation: The defender and teammate create the choice. A lane only becomes useful if it remains open after the movement.

questions.prompt: Arrange this shooting-lane read.

options.text: Identify D1 and F2
Check whether a lane or pass opens
Choose a shot, pass or protected touch

questions.explanation: Check the current lane and support, then choose among the available options. You do not have to wait for D1 to move.

questions.prompt: Move YOU sideways to change the shooting angle around D1.
questions.explanation: The example moves the carrier and puck sideways and changes the line to the net. Recheck D1, the goalie and F2; the position does not prove an open shot.

questions.prompt: Imagine D1 moves onto the passing line to F2 and away from the shooting line. YOU still control the puck. Which option has gained space from D1?

options.text: A shot toward the net
A direct pass to F2

questions.explanation: In this stated change, D1 has moved away from the shot line and into the pass line. A shot is therefore worth reassessing, but control, the goalie and any further movement still matter. It is not a guaranteed goal, and another option may become useful if the picture changes.

questions.prompt: How do your position and F2’s wider position offer different choices?
questions.explanation: YOU have a central shooting line with D1 in it; F2 offers a wider passing option. Compare those routes and explain what must stay open before using either.

scenes.title: Backcheck the open runner
scenes.objective: Choose a backcheck relationship for the uncovered attacker while a teammate pressures the puck.
scenes.briefing: Gold attacks the left net (-x), defended by navy. In this rep, navy D1 is assigned to pressure gold F1, who owns the puck. Gold F2 trails across the middle. YOU start closer to the left net than F2 and must scan that runner while checking whether D1 can maintain pressure.
cues: D1 is assigned puck pressure; the freeze does not prove successful pressure.
F2 is a separate trailing gold attacker.
YOU start closer to the left net than F2, at the same up-ice coordinate as F1.

questions.prompt: Who has the puck-pressure assignment in this rep?

options.text: YOU
D1
F2

questions.explanation: The briefing assigns navy D1 to pressure gold F1. Whether D1 can stay with F1 remains part of the read.

questions.prompt: What belongs in your backcheck read?

options.text: F2’s route toward the left net
D1's ability to stay with F1
The puck alone, without scanning F2

questions.explanation: The uncovered runner toward the left net and D1’s pressure on F1 define the backcheck job.

questions.prompt: Arrange this backcheck check-in.

options.text: Find F2 and the left net
Skate into a useful relationship
Re-check F1, F2 and D1

questions.explanation: Look for a relationship that limits the runner’s passing or shooting options, then update as D1’s pressure changes.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward F2 while staying between F2 and the left net.
questions.explanation: This point closes the distance to F2 while staying on the net side of F2's route, without pretending that one spot solves the play.

questions.prompt: If YOU consider helping D1 elsewhere, which attacker is currently on YOUR side of the middle and must stay in the read?

options.text: F1
F2

questions.explanation: YOU and F2 are on the same side of the middle; F1 is across it with the puck. YOU also start closer to the defended left net than F2. Account for that runner if discussing help with D1, rather than assuming a particular switch is required.

questions.prompt: How is a backcheck different from simply skating toward the puck?
questions.explanation: It connects your route to an attacker and the net, so you can limit a pass or shot while reading the teammate pressure.
